output.brief:
Cancellations are mostly not a pricing problem. Accounts connected to Quillbook are the ones leaving: their monthly churn rose from about 2% to about 6%, whether they were repriced or on the locked Founders price. Accounts with no connector, which is most of the base and includes repriced accounts at every size, stayed at about 1.9%. The cause appears to be Quillbook retiring its old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or doubled invoices. That affected 1,212 accounts, and 34% of them have cancelled, against 8% of unaffected accounts. The health panel doesn't count these events, and the fix is rated low priority. The earlier price-size pattern comes from Quillbook accounts having more seats. Slow support responses likely add to the damage, but I can't show that on its own.

What to do: make the Quillbook v3 fix the top engineering priority (about 3–4 weeks). Contact every Quillbook account, including those who cancelled, to correct their invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on. Don't roll back the price. Hold off on the Tallymarsh rebuild; have someone review its log first. Confidence is high on the Quillbook finding. The Tallymarsh and support-speed questions remain open.
